## pencil
The Pencil MCP server is the editor for .pen design files (web/mobile apps and websites). Use it to read, generate, and validate designs.

.pen files are encrypted: access them only via "pencil" MCP tools — never use Read or Grep on .pen files. Follow each tool's input schema exactly.

Always call get_editor_state(include_schema: true) if you don't have the current .pen file schema in the context. Knowing the schema is required to use any other Pencil MCP tool.

Tools: get_editor_state, get_guidelines, batch_get, batch_design, snapshot_layout, get_screenshot, get_variables, export_nodes, export_html.

- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

content.text:
Read it. My call: **jump straight to planning.**

Phase 72 is a debt-cleanup phase, not a design-space-open one. All 6 success criteria are already concrete and each maps 1:1 to a specific pending todo — fail-closed behavior, dropping a ref, re-homing on restore, mirror refresh, dead-branch removal, helper dedup. There's no architectural fork here; the "what" is pinned down, only the "how" remains, which is planning's job.

The one thing worth a beat before you plan — not a full discuss — is **SC#2 (fail-closed on transient resolve miss)**. "Fails closed" needs a decided error-surfacing contract: throw vs. return an error result, and whether the caller (upload/move flow) already has a retry path or will now hard-fail a previously-silent operation. That's the only SC where a wrong guess ripples into web/UX. The rest are mechanical.

Recommendation: `/gsd-plan-phase 72`, and let the planner nail down the SC#2 error contract as part of the plan. Want me to kick that off?

**Goal**: The web app preserves write capability and fresh listings when navigating shared folders — nested write-shares keep their writeKey across navigate-up/breadcrumb restore, the nav-stack no longer serves stale child snapshots, the non-listing read facades are floor-gated, WRITE-03 refresh-access has a real production trigger, and drag-payload kind comes from the resolved listing.

1. Navigating up / restoring a breadcrumb into a nested write-share retains the derived writeKey (navStack entries carry the writeKey, not only `folderKey`); a write into a deep shared subfolder succeeds after breadcrumb restore

5. `SharedFolderRow` drag-payload kind is derived from the resolved listing (`isFileRefResolved`/`resolvedByIpnsName`), not `isFileRef` on a bare `SealedChildRef`

content.text:
Checked the file targets — there's a **real dependency, not just conservative ordering**. Answer: **not cleanly parallel; sequence 72 → 73.**

The coupling is `packages/sdk/src/client.ts`, which both phases modify heavily:

- **Phase 72** refactors the write primitives in `client.ts` — `getWriteBodyParams` (fail-closed rewrite), the write-plane helper dedup (lines 851/2825), plus delete/rehome/mirror edits scattered across the file.
- **Phase 73** lands on the *same* primitives: SC#4 (WRITE-03 live trigger) wires a tombstone into `buildSharedWriteContextFromState` / `publishNodeFn` — which sits directly on top of the `getWriteBodyParams` write-body-build code 72 is rewriting. SC#3 (floor-gate read facades) and the 68.2 item also edit `client.ts`.

Doing both at once means textual conflicts *and* semantic churn on the exact functions 72 is reshaping. That's why the roadmap's `73 depends on 72` is right.

**But 73 splits cleanly.** Three of its five SCs are pure `apps/web` and touch nothing 72 owns:
- SC#1/#2 — navStack writeKey preservation + stale-snapshot invalidation (`useSharedNavigationActions.ts`)
- SC#5 — drag-kind (`SharedFolderRow.tsx`)

Only SC#3 (floor-gate) and SC#4 (refresh trigger) + the 68.2 SDK item ride on `client.ts` and must wait for 72.

<objective>
Create executable phase prompts (PLAN.md files) for a roadmap phase with integrated research and verification.

**Default flow:** Research (if needed) → Plan → Verify → Done

**Research-only mode (`--research-phase <N>`):** Spawn `gsd-phase-researcher` for phase `N`, write `RESEARCH.md`, then exit before the planner runs. Useful for cross-phase research, doc review before committing to a planning approach, and correction-without-replanning loops where iterating on research alone is dramatically cheaper than re-spawning the planner. Replaces the deleted research-phase command (#3042).

**Research-only modifiers:**
- **No flag** — when `RESEARCH.md` already exists, auto-uses it: emits a one-line notice and exits cleanly, no prompt.
- **`--research`** — force-refresh: re-spawn the researcher unconditionally, no prompt. Bypasses the existing-RESEARCH.md auto-use path.
- **`--view`** — view-only: print existing `RESEARCH.md` to stdout. Does not spawn the researcher. Cheapest mode for the correction-without-replanning loop. If no `RESEARCH.md` exists yet, errors with a hint to drop `--view`.

**Orchestrator role:** Parse arguments, validate phase, research domain (unless skipped), spawn gsd-planner, verify with gsd-plan-checker, iterate until pass or max iterations, present results.
</objective>

<ui_patterns>

Visual patterns for user-facing GSD output. Orchestrators @-reference this file.

## Stage Banners

Use for major workflow transitions.

```
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
 GSD ► {STAGE NAME}
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
```

**Stage names (uppercase):**
- `QUESTIONING`
- `RESEARCHING`
- `DEFINING REQUIREMENTS`
- `CREATING ROADMAP`
- `PLANNING PHASE {N}`
- `EXECUTING WAVE {N}`
- `VERIFYING`
- `PHASE {N} COMPLETE ✓`
- `MILESTONE COMPLETE 🎉`

---

## Checkpoint Boxes

User action required. 62-character width.

```
╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║  CHECKPOINT: {Type}                                          ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝

{Content}

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
→ {ACTION PROMPT}
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

**Types:**
- `CHECKPOINT: Verification Required` → `→ Type "approved" or describe issues`
- `CHECKPOINT: Decision Required` → `→ Select: option-a / option-b`
- `CHECKPOINT: Action Required` → `→ Type "done" when complete`

---

## Status Symbols

```
✓  Complete / Passed / Verified
✗  Failed / Missing / Blocked
◆  In Progress
○  Pending
⚡ Auto-approved
⚠  Warning
🎉 Milestone complete (only in banner)
```

---

## Progress Display

**Phase/milestone level:**
```
Progress: ████████░░ 80%
```

**Task level:**
```
Tasks: 2/4 complete
```

**Plan level:**
```
Plans: 3/5 complete
```

---

## Spawning Indicators

**Liveness convention:** Every spawn announcement must carry the canonical phrase `runs in a subagent` inline so users know that silence during a subagent run is expected. Without this, a healthy 1–5 minute agent looks identical to a frozen session. Single spawns use the singular form; parallel spawns use the plural form.

```
◆ Spawning researcher... (runs in a subagent — no output until it returns, ~1–5 min; expected, not a freeze)

◆ Spawning 4 researchers in parallel... (each runs in a subagent — no output until they return, ~1–5 min; expected, not a freeze)
  → Stack research
  → Features research
  → Architecture research
  → Pitfalls research

✓ Researcher complete: STACK.md written
```

---

## Next Up Block

Always at end of major completions.

```
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

## ▶ Next Up

**{Identifier}: {Name}** — {one-line description}

`/clear` then:

`{copy-paste command}`

───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

**Also available:**
- `/gsd-alternative-1` — description
- `/gsd-alternative-2` — description

───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

---

## Error Box

```
╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║  ERROR                                                       ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝

{Error description}

**To fix:** {Resolution steps}
```

---

## Tables

```
| Phase | Status | Plans | Progress |
|-------|--------|-------|----------|
| 1     | ✓      | 3/3   | 100%     |
| 2     | ◆      | 1/4   | 25%      |
| 3     | ○      | 0/2   | 0%       |
```

---

## Anti-Patterns

- Varying box/banner widths
- Mixing banner styles (`===`, `---`, `***`)
- Skipping `GSD ►` prefix in banners
- Random emoji (`🚀`, `✨`, `💫`)
- Missing Next Up block after completions

</ui_patterns>

The Agent tool IS available in a top-level Claude Code session. Always spawn
gsd-phase-researcher, gsd-planner, and gsd-plan-checker as separate Agent() calls.
Never absorb these roles inline. Role separation is required regardless of `--chain`
or `--auto` — those options suppress interactive prompts only; they NEVER authorize
collapsing plan roles into the orchestrator context.

**Backgrounded Claude Code (via manager/autonomous):**
The calling workflow (manager.md / autonomous.md) already runs plan-phase inline via
Skill() on Claude Code so that the plan-checker subagent can still spawn. plan-phase
itself does not need to detect this case.

**#1009 caveat (discuss-phase early-exit):**
The "display the command and exit" instruction near `## 4` applies only to the
discuss-phase early-exit path. It does NOT authorize inline role performance for any
plan-phase agents.

**Other runtimes:**
Do not pre-judge Agent availability by introspection. Always attempt the actual
Agent() call for gsd-phase-researcher, gsd-planner, and gsd-plan-checker. Only
a real tool-unavailable error returned by Agent() is a reliable absence signal —
never stop based on a self-assessed "I think Agent is unavailable." If the call
fails with a tool-unavailable error, log the gap and stop — do NOT collapse
researcher/planner/checker roles inline. Independent agent contexts are required
for the plan-checker gate to be meaningful.

<process>

## 1.5. Closed-Phase Gate (#3569)

The init JSON includes `phase_status` — one of `Pending | Planned | In Progress | Executed | Complete | Needs Review`. `Complete` means the phase has all summaries AND a `VERIFICATION.md` with `status: passed`. Replanning a closed phase silently rewrites plan docs that no longer match the shipped code, so the workflow must hard-stop here unless the operator explicitly overrides.

Parse `phase_status` from the init JSON, then:

```bash
FORCE_REPLAN=false
if [[ "$ARGUMENTS" =~ (^|[[:space:]])--force([[:space:]]|$) ]]; then
  FORCE_REPLAN=true
fi

if [ "${phase_status}" = "Complete" ]; then
  if [[ "$ARGUMENTS" =~ (^|[[:space:]])--reviews([[:space:]]|$) ]]; then
    # --reviews on a closed phase is never legitimate — concerns belong in a
    # new phase or issue against the closed phase's commits.
    cat <<EOF >&2
Phase ${phase_number} (${phase_name}) is already CLOSED (VERIFICATION status: passed).
/gsd-plan-phase --reviews cannot replan a closed phase. If the review surfaced
real concerns, open a follow-up phase or file an issue against the closed
phase's commits. There is no --force override for --reviews on a closed phase.
EOF
    exit 1
  fi
  if [ "$FORCE_REPLAN" != "true" ]; then
    cat <<EOF >&2
Phase ${phase_number} (${phase_name}) is already CLOSED (VERIFICATION status: passed).
Replanning a closed phase will overwrite plan docs that no longer match the
shipped code. If you intentionally want to replan over closed work, re-run
with: /gsd-plan-phase ${phase_number} --force

Otherwise, to view what shipped, see: ${verification_path}
EOF
    exit 1
  fi
  # FORCE_REPLAN=true: continue, but emit a banner so the operator sees the
  # decision in the transcript and in any committed plan docs.
  echo "WARNING: Replanning CLOSED phase ${phase_number} under --force. Verify the closeout was wrong before committing new plan docs." >&2
fi
```

The gate fires only on `Complete`. `Executed` and `Needs Review` are not gated — those states mean planning was finished but verification did not pass, and replanning is a legitimate next step.

Extract from $ARGUMENTS: phase number (integer or decimal like `2.1`), flags (`--research`, `--skip-research`, `--research-phase <N>`, `--gaps`, `--skip-verify`, `--skip-ui`, `--prd <filepath>`, `--ingest <path-or-glob>`, `--ingest-format <auto|nygard|madr|narrative>`, `--reviews`, `--text`, `--bounce`, `--skip-bounce`, `--chunked`, `--mvp`, `--tdd`, `--granularity <coarse|standard|fine>`, `--force` (override closed-phase gate, see §1.5)).

**`--research-phase <N>` — research-only mode (#3042 + #3044).** When this flag is present, parse `<N>` as the phase number (overrides any positional phase argument), set `RESEARCH_ONLY=true`, and treat the rest of this workflow as a research-dispatch only — the planner spawn (step 8), plan-checker, verification, gaps, bounce, and post-planning-gaps blocks all skip on `RESEARCH_ONLY`. Use this for cross-phase research, doc review before committing to a planning approach, and correction-without-replanning loops. Replaces the deleted `/gsd-research-phase` command.

In research-only mode, two modifiers control behavior when `RESEARCH.md` already exists:

- **`--research`** — force-refresh re-research without prompting. Re-spawns the researcher unconditionally and overwrites the existing RESEARCH.md. (This is the existing `--research` flag's standard "force re-research" semantics, reused here.)
- **`--view`** — view-only: print existing `RESEARCH.md` to stdout, do **not** spawn the researcher. Sets `VIEW_ONLY=true`. Cheapest mode for the correction-without-replanning loop. If `RESEARCH.md` does not exist, error with a hint to drop `--view`.

```bash

VIEW_ONLY=false

  RESEARCH_ONLY=true
  PHASE="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"

**`--granularity <coarse|standard|fine>` — CLI override (#703).** When present, this value is the resolved granularity passed to the planner — it wins over any per-phase `granularities.<type>` config, top-level `granularity` config, or project defaults. The init JSON always includes a `granularity` field reflecting the resolved value; read it from there. Invalid values (anything other than `coarse`, `standard`, `fine`) cause an error at the CLI boundary.

Set `TEXT_MODE=true` if `--text` is present in $ARGUMENTS OR `text_mode` from init JSON is `true`. **MVP_MODE resolution.** Resolve `MVP_MODE` once via the centralized `phase.mvp-mode` query verb. Precedence (first hit wins): CLI flag → ROADMAP.md `**Mode:** mvp` → `workflow.mvp_mode` config → false. The verb is the single source of truth — do not re-implement the chain.

```bash
MVP_FLAG_ARG=""
if [[ "$ARGUMENTS" =~ (^|[[:space:]])--mvp([[:space:]]|$) ]]; then MVP_FLAG_ARG="--cli-flag"; fi

The verb returns `true|false`; full result also exposes `source` (`cli_flag` | `roadmap` | `config` | `none`) for diagnostics. Mode is **all-or-nothing per phase** (PRD decision Q1).

**Walking Skeleton gate.** When `MVP_MODE=true` AND `phase_number == "01"` AND there are zero prior phase summaries (new project), the planner runs in **Walking Skeleton mode** (per PRD decision Q2 — new projects only). Detect with:

```bash
WALKING_SKELETON=false
if [ "$MVP_MODE" = "true" ] && [ "$padded_phase" = "01" ]; then
  PRIOR_SUMMARIES=$(gsd_run query phases.list --pick summaries_total 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
  if [ "$PRIOR_SUMMARIES" = "0" ]; then WALKING_SKELETON=true; fi
fi
```

When `WALKING_SKELETON=true`:
- Planner is instructed to produce `SKELETON.md` in the phase directory alongside `PLAN.md`. The template lives at `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/.claude/gsd-core/references/skeleton-template.md` — the planner reads it when producing SKELETON.md (lazy; not loaded on non-skeleton runs).
- The plan must scaffold project + routing + one real DB read/write + one real UI interaction + dev deployment — the thinnest possible end-to-end working slice.

**Interaction with `--prd <filepath>`.** `--mvp` and `--prd` compose. The PRD express path (Step 3.5) creates `CONTEXT.md` from the PRD file and continues to research; the Walking Skeleton gate fires independently from the conditions above. When both are active on Phase 1 of a new project, the planner receives `WALKING_SKELETON=true` and PRD-derived context simultaneously — the PRD informs *what the skeleton should prove*. No precedence is needed; the two signals are orthogonal. See [`references/mvp-concepts.md`](../references/mvp-concepts.md) for the broader interaction map.

## Problem

In BOTH `getWriteBodyParams` copies (client.ts ~669 and bin/index.ts ~72), a
TRANSIENT IPNS resolve miss on an already-write-capable folder returns
`writeChildren: []` (the D-03 fail-open path). If the folder then republishes, it
seals an EMPTY write-body — dropping the entire write chain (every child's
WriteChildRef), not just failing read-only. Distinct from the intended
read-only-device fallback (zero writeKey): here the device HAS the writeKey but a
network blip erased the children list it should have preserved.

This is a documented D-03 fail-open and is identical in both files, so it was NOT
one-sidedly flipped during ship (flipping only the bin copy would diverge the two).
It needs a holistic decision.

## Solution

Decide the fail-open-vs-fail-closed contract for a transient resolve miss when a
real writeKey is present, then apply it to BOTH copies together (or dedupe them —
see [[dedupe-sdk-write-plane-helpers]]). Options: (a) fail-closed — throw/retry
rather than publish an empty write-body when writeKey is present but the resolve
missed; (b) preserve the last-known local writeChildren mirror across a transient
miss (mirrors the 68.1-23 network-refresh preservation). Gate with sdk unit suites
+ a concurrent-operations sdk-e2e run that injects a resolve failure.

created: 2026-07-10
title: Zero file read/write keys when a later unwrap throws in updateSharedSingleFile
area: crypto
files:
  - packages/sdk/src/client.ts
---

## Problem

In `SdkClient.updateSharedSingleFile` (packages/sdk/src/client.ts ~5312-5319), both
`fileReadKey` and `fileWriteKey` are produced by `unwrapKey(...)` BEFORE the `try` block
that owns the `finally { fileReadKey?.fill(0); fileWriteKey?.fill(0); }` cleanup. If the
SECOND `unwrapKey` (fileWriteKey) throws, the already-unwrapped `fileReadKey` never reaches
the `finally` and lingers un-zeroed in the heap until GC.

Pre-existing (the try-block structure is unchanged by Phase 71; only the field name on the
adjacent `hexToBytes(args.encryptedReadKey)` line was renamed). Flagged by CodeRabbit on the
Phase 71 diff. Low severity (hygiene, not a direct exploit) — deferred to keep the Phase 71
PR scoped to the share-plane rename + security/data-integrity work.

## Solution

Initialize `fileReadKey`/`fileWriteKey` to `null` before the `try`, and move BOTH `unwrapKey`
calls inside the `try` so any failure reaches the existing `finally` cleanup:

```ts
let fileReadKey: Uint8Array | null = null;
let fileWriteKey: Uint8Array | null = null;
let currentFileNode: CoreNode | null = null;
try {
  fileReadKey = await unwrapKey(hexToBytes(args.encryptedReadKey), args.recipientPrivateKey);
  fileWriteKey = await unwrapKey(hexToBytes(args.encryptedWriteKey), args.recipientPrivateKey);
  ...
```

Validate with `packages/sdk/src/__tests__/update-shared-single-file.test.ts`.

I have everything needed. Confirmed: the equivocation gate was added in #599 at `apps/api/src/ipns/ipns.service.ts:345`, absent in the parent commit.

## Diagnosis Report: desktop-e2e failure on run 29059796208

### Verdict: REAL REGRESSION (not a flake), introduced by the failing commit itself (#599)

Both macOS (job 86259026967) and Linux (job 86259026982) fail on the **same test, same step, same error** — the hallmark of a real code regression, not an environmental/flake issue.

### 1. Failing test (identical on both OSes)

- Test: **"Shared scope-exit rotation acceptance (D-16)" → Part A: shared scope-exit rotation**
- Script: `tests/desktop-e2e/scripts/shared-scope-exit-rotation.mts:295`
- Surface error (both OSes): `AxiosError: Request failed with status code 400`
- Root-cause error from the FUSE crate log (both OSes), e.g. macOS ino 2:
  > `Per-file node publish failed for ino 2: API returned error 400: IPNS publish failed: {"message":"Same-sequence republish with a different CID rejected (equivocation): stored=bafkrei...samji, incoming=bafkrei...47qxa, sequence=1","error":"Bad Request","statusCode":400}`

  Linux hits the identical rejection (`stored=...ttbya, incoming=...nmwpi, sequence=1`).

Windows failed separately on an infra step ("Setup PostgreSQL", postgres-version validation) — unrelated to the regression. Web E2E also failed but is a separate pre-existing failure (Web E2E has been red since before this run).

### 2. Flake ruled out

The known ~15% macOS flake is **cross-client-sync Test 5 (FUSE-T/SMB cache)**. That is not what failed here — both OSes fail deterministically at the D-16 rotation step on an API 400, and Linux (no FUSE-T) fails identically. No mount/linking failure either — the mount succeeded (`FUSE mount confirmed at /Users/runner/CipherBox`).

### 3. Culprit commit: #599 (703bc0083)

`feat: enforce share-invite authorization and IPNS data-integrity in the API`, headSha `703bc0083`, event push on main.

The equivocation gate that emits the 400 was **added by this exact commit** in `apps/api/src/ipns/ipns.service.ts:345`:
```
Same-sequence republish with a different CID rejected (equivocation): stored=${existing.latestCid}, incoming=${metadataCid}, sequence=${dbSeq}
```
`git grep` confirms the string is present at 703bc0083 but **absent in the parent commit d5486e586**. The desktop FUSE per-file node publish path republishes at `sequence=1` with a different metadata CID, which this new API gate now rejects with 400 — breaking the D-16 acceptance test.

(desktop-e2e ran on this "API" PR because the desktop FUSE stack exercises the live IPNS publish API; the `apps/api/src/ipns` change tripped the Detect Changes filter.)

### 4. Persistent, not intermittent — and freshly regressed

Desktop E2E status on recent main runs:
- **29059796208 (#599)** — macOS FAIL, Linux FAIL, Windows infra-fail ← this run
- 29011170677 (#598, rotation read-plane) — Desktop macOS/Linux/Windows all **PASS** (only Web E2E failed)
- 28941806263 (#596, rotation soundness) — Desktop all 3 **PASS** (only Web E2E failed)
- 28882899171 (#594, FUSE/WinFsp integration) — all green

So the D-16 test passed as recently as ~14h ago (#598) and regressed exactly at #599. It is a hard, deterministic regression — it will stay red on every subsequent desktop-e2e run until the API equivocation gate is reconciled with the FUSE same-sequence republish behavior (either the gate should not reject an identical-intent republish, or the FUSE publish path must bump the sequence / send a matching CID).

Key files: `apps/api/src/ipns/ipns.service.ts` (the new gate, ~line 345), `tests/desktop-e2e/scripts/shared-scope-exit-rotation.mts` (line 295, the failing assertion), and the FUSE publish caller `crates/fuse/src/read_ops/implementation.rs` (emits "Per-file node publish failed for ino ...").

content.text:
Investigation complete. Here's the report.

## Web-e2e failure diagnosis — run 28941806263 (#596)

**Run under investigation**
- SHA `faa781e4164697b17cc7765624985dcb9a38f761`, branch `main`, title `fix: harden rotation soundness under concurrency and crash-resume (#596)`.
- In this run only `Web E2E / Web E2E Tests` (job 85865671229) failed; all 3 desktop-e2e OSes passed.

### 1. Failing spec + exact error (target run #596)
Exactly one test failed — the very first setup step of the writable-shares suite:

```
1) [chromium] › tests/writable-shares.spec.ts:123:3 › Writable Shares › 1.1 Create test accounts (Alice, Bob)
   TimeoutError: page.waitForURL: Timeout 90000ms exceeded.
   > 185 | page.waitForURL('**/files', { timeout }).then(() => ({ outcome: 'success' }))
     at attemptWalletLogin (tests/web-e2e/utils/wallet-login-helpers.ts:185:10)
     at loginViaWallet (.../wallet-login-helpers.ts:241:14)
     at createWalletTestAccount (.../multi-account-wallet.ts:77:20)
     at tests/writable-shares.spec.ts:126:11

   1 failed / 184 passed (14.5m)
```

Line 185 is the post–"Mock Wallet" click race that waits for **either** a `**/files` redirect **or** the `device-waiting` screen — neither appeared within 90s.

The `duplicate key ... UQ_ipns_records_ipns_name` DB errors and `[cleanup] Account deletion failed at refresh: HTTP 401` lines in the log are expected/handled test noise (concurrency-test inserts + teardown), not the failure. Homebrew tap warnings are also noise.

### 2. Hard-fail vs flake — VERDICT: FLAKE (one-off)
- It's the account-creation wallet login, not any assertion about product behavior. It matches the known **Web3Auth Core Kit login flake** signature (mock-wallet login never redirects to `/files` within timeout).
- It is the first test in the file, so the rest of `writable-shares` cascade-aborted — but the signature is purely login-timeout.
- `writable-shares.spec.ts` **passed** in both subsequent runs (#598, #599), confirming this specific failure did not recur → one-off flake.

### 3. Culprit commit hypothesis
Not a code regression from #596. The failing spec exercises wallet account creation, which is unrelated to the rotation-soundness changes in `faa781e4`. `rotation-durability.spec.ts` (the spec touched by that phase's area) **passed** in this run. Culprit = infra/Web3Auth login timeout, not `faa781e4`.

### 4. Is web-e2e still red on main? YES — but for a DIFFERENT, persistent reason
web-e2e on `main` is currently failing, and it is **not** the #596 login flake. The two most recent runs fail on a newer, recurring regression:

- **#598** (`d5486e58`, run 29011170677): 2 failed / 208 passed
  - `rotation-durability.spec.ts:193:3 › seeds the durable high-water floor (create + rename, SC#4 setup)`
  - `full-workflow.spec.ts:1456:3 › 8.2 Delete remaining root files`
- **#599** (`703bc008`, run 29059796208): 1 failed / 210 passed
  - `rotation-durability.spec.ts:193:3 › seeds the durable high-water floor (create + rename, SC#4 setup)`

The recurring failure signature:
```
Error: expect(received).toBeDefined()
Received: undefined
  216 | expect(floors.generation).toBeDefined();
  const floors = await readDurableFloors(page, rootIpnsName);
  at tests/web-e2e/tests/rotation-durability.spec.ts:216:31
```
`readDurableFloors()` returns an object whose `generation` is `undefined` after a real UI create+rename mutation — i.e. the durable IndexedDB high-water floor isn't being persisted as the spec expects. This spec existed and **passed** at #596, so the regression was introduced by the rotation read-plane durability hardening landed in **#598 (`d5486e58`)** and persists through #599. `full-workflow 8.2` in #598 looks like an additional flake (didn't recur in #599).

### Bottom line
- The run you asked about (#596) is a **one-off Web3Auth wallet-login flake** on `writable-shares 1.1`, unrelated to the #596 code.
- However, **main's web-e2e is now persistently red on a real regression**: `rotation-durability.spec.ts:193` (`floors.generation` undefined), introduced by the rotation read-plane durability work in #598 and still failing on latest main (#599). That is the item worth acting on, not the #596 flake.

Relevant files:
- `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/tests/web-e2e/utils/wallet-login-helpers.ts:185` (flake site)
- `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/tests/web-e2e/tests/rotation-durability.spec.ts:216` (persistent regression assertion)

Both diagnosed. There are **two separate real regressions on main** (not flakes), each from one of the phases we just discussed retiring todos for:

## 1. Desktop-e2e (macos + linux) — regressed at #599 (Phase 71)
- **Root cause:** Phase 71's new IPNS anti-equivocation gate (`apps/api/src/ipns/ipns.service.ts:345`) rejects "same-sequence republish with a different CID" with a 400.
- The FUSE per-file node publish path republishes at **sequence=1 with a different metadata CID** (a rotation re-key changes the CID), which the new gate now rejects → D-16 `shared-scope-exit-rotation` test fails identically on both OSes.
- Deterministic, both OSes, same test/step/error — a genuine regression. Passed at #598, red since #599. (Windows failed separately on a postgres-setup infra step — unrelated.)

## 2. Web-e2e — regressed at #598 (Phase 70.1)
- **Root cause:** `rotation-durability.spec.ts:216` — `floors.generation` is `undefined` after a real UI create+rename. The durable IndexedDB high-water floor isn't persisted in the shape the spec reads.
- Introduced by Phase 70.1's rotation read-plane durability work (touched `packages/sdk/src/state/rotation-high-water.ts`), persists through #599.
- (The #596 run you first linked was actually a one-off Web3Auth login flake — but web-e2e *is* persistently red, for this #598 reason.)

**Assessment:** These are two independent fixes touching shipped code. The desktop one is a real API↔FUSE contract collision — Phase 71's gate is correct in principle (anti-equivocation is a security guarantee), so the fix is most likely on the FUSE side (bump the sequence when the CID changes) rather than relaxing the gate. The web one is a durability/serialization mismatch in the floor store. Both should land as separate small fix PRs, and green main matters before we build Phase 72/73 on top of it (otherwise new branches inherit red CI signal).

I'd pause Phase 72 planning, fix both regressions first. Before I dig into the exact fixes, one call is yours:

The FUSE per-file node publish path emits: "Per-file node publish failed for ino N: API returned error 400: IPNS publish failed: Same-sequence republish with a different CID rejected (equivocation): stored=<cidA>, incoming=<cidB>, sequence=1".

The 400 comes from a Phase 71 anti-equivocation gate added in commit 703bc0083 at apps/api/src/ipns/ipns.service.ts:~345 — that gate is CORRECT and must stay. The bug is on the FUSE side: during a shared scope-exit rotation re-key, the per-file node's metadata changes (new sealed keys → new CID), but FUSE republishes it at sequence=1 (the first-publish sequence) instead of bumping to the next sequence via the CAS path. A stored record already exists at seq=1, so the new-CID-at-seq=1 publish is (correctly) rejected as equivocation.

DECISION ALREADY MADE: fix the FUSE publish path (bump the sequence / route the re-key republish through the CAS/subsequent-publish path), NOT relax the API gate.

Project context (from memory, verify against code): "Every first IPNS publish must embed sequence 1; strict gate rejects first publish with seq≠1. createAndPublishIpnsRecord passes 1n, publishWithCas passes 0n." So there is a distinction between first-publish (seq=1) and CAS/subsequent publish (bump). The re-key republish is a SUBSEQUENT publish and must not reuse the first-publish seq=1 path.

Your investigation:
1. Find the FUSE "Per-file node publish" call site. Grep crates/fuse for the "Per-file node publish failed for ino" string and trace back to the publish call. Likely crates/fuse/src/read_ops/implementation.rs, but confirm. Identify the function that does the shared scope-exit rotation re-key + publish.
2. Determine EXACTLY how the sequence number is chosen on that path — where does seq=1 come from? Is it hardcoded, or is it resolving current sequence and defaulting to 1 on a miss, or routing through a first-publish helper instead of a CAS helper?
3. Compare to how a NORMAL per-file metadata update publishes (the working path that correctly bumps sequence). Find the CAS/bump publish helper the FUSE code already has and uses elsewhere. The fix should reuse the existing correct path.

Note any signature/threading changes needed. Flag whether this is Rust-only or also touches a TS/bin helper.
5. Note how to validate locally (the D-16 script is .mts + needs the local stack; also whether `cargo test`/`cargo check` covers it, and that Windows is CI-only).

Return: exact bug location (file:line + code excerpt), why seq=1 is emitted, the existing correct CAS path to reuse, and a concrete minimal patch proposal with the actual code change. Be precise — quote the real code.

## Problem

The D-16 desktop-e2e leg `shared-scope-exit-rotation.mts` has been red on `main` since #599, failing identically on macOS and Linux:

```
Per-file node publish failed for ino N: API returned error 400:
IPNS publish failed: Same-sequence republish with a different CID rejected
(equivocation): stored=<cidA>, incoming=<cidB>, sequence=1
```

The 400 comes from Phase 71's anti-equivocation gate (`apps/api/src/ipns/ipns.service.ts`, #599) — which is **correct and stays intact**. The bug is on the FUSE side.

## Root cause

`publish_file_node` (`crates/fuse/src/content_ops.rs`) took its **seq-1 first-publish** tail purely on the caller's `is_first_publish` hint, which is `true` whenever the file inode's CID is empty (`read_ops.rs`). That inode CID is only filled by the `UploadComplete` drain, which is guarded by `write_generation` (`fs.rs`). A dropped completion (a superseding write bumps the generation) or a duplicated/deferred FUSE-T `release` leaves the inode CID empty, so a later release re-runs the seq-1 tail. Each run re-seals a **fresh** node envelope (`created_at`/`modified_at = now_ms` change → new envelope CID). Two seq-1 publishes with different CIDs is exactly the equivocation the Phase 71 gate rejects. The rotation window's extra mount activity makes this reliably observable in D-16.

## Fix (Rust-only)

Resolve the per-file IPNS name before the first-publish tail:

- `NotFound` → genuine first publish: seq 1 + TEE enrollment (unchanged).
- `Found` → the record already exists; the changed content still needs publishing, so fall through to the existing sequence-bumping CAS branch (`publish_with_cas_retry`) — no seq-1 equivocation.
- `Error` → fail the release closed rather than risk a seq-1 equivocation.

This mirrors the resolve-first guard already used by `replay.rs::publish_child_node` (which *skips* on `Found` because replay has nothing new to publish — here we do, so we route to CAS). `publish_file_node` is the single shared entry point for fuser (macOS/Linux) and WinFsp, so one edit fixes all three platforms. TEE enrollment stays on the genuine-first-publish path (crypto rule 7).

I have everything needed. Here is my diagnosis.

## Verdict: PR-independent flake rooted in Phase 71 (#599) — NOT caused by PR #600

PR #600's failure of "SDK E2E Tests" cannot be caused by its diff (a single Playwright web-e2e file), and the evidence confirms it: the failing test is a **new, inherently racy D-06 concurrency test introduced by #599 (Phase 71)** that flaked red.

## 1. Exact failing test + error signature

**Suite/test:** `tests/sdk-e2e/src/suites/ipns-publish-gate.test.ts`
> `IPNS publish-gate suite (TEE-04/07, WRITE-04 phase gate) > Test 21 (D-06): concurrent first-publish of the same new ipnsName → exactly one 200 + one 409`

**Error (quoted from run 29061490828 / job 86264251246):**
```
AssertionError: expected [ { status: 'fulfilled', …(1) }, …(1) ] to have a length of 1 but got 2
  408|     expect(fulfilled).toHaveLength(1);
Test Files  1 failed | 15 passed (16)
      Tests  1 failed | 104 passed (105)
```
Only 1 of 105 tests failed. **Both** concurrent first-publish calls resolved `fulfilled` (200) instead of the expected one-200 + one-409.

## 2. Root cause — Phase 71 idempotency vs. the test's expectation

The test (lines 367-413) fires two concurrent `createAndPublishIpnsRecord` calls for the same brand-new `ipnsName`, **both carrying the identical CID `bafybeigdyrzt5…` and `sequenceNumber: 1n`**. It expects the INSERT-race loser to get a `23505` unique-violation translated to a clean 409.

But Phase 71's anti-equivocation gate only rejects a same-sequence republish when the **CID differs**. Here both CIDs are identical, so a same-sequence/same-CID republish is treated as an **idempotent success (200)**. The outcome is timing-dependent:
- If the second request's INSERT collides mid-flight → 409 (test passes).
- If it serializes *after* the first commits, it re-reads an existing record with identical CID+sequence and returns idempotent 200 → **two fulfilled → test fails.**

This is a genuine non-deterministic race, not a stack-health issue. It is the **same Phase 71 lineage** as the desktop breakage (both are downstream of the #599 IPNS-integrity gate), but this is a flaky-test/edge-semantics interaction, not the gate wrongly 400-ing legitimate traffic.

## 3. Reproduction across PRs/main — proves it's not #600

- **#599's own PR run** (29059417349): SDK E2E **passed** (2m44s) — the race won by luck on the run that *introduced* the test.
- **#600 PR run** (29061490828): SDK E2E **failed** on Test 21 — same test, different timing.
- **#601** (fuse-only): SDK E2E is **skipped** (`skipping`) — path-filter gates it off, so #601 can't corroborate.
- **Main pushes:** SDK E2E does **not run on main** (path-gated). Confirmed absent on the last 3 main CI-E2E runs (29059796208 #599-merge, 29011170677, 28941806263). The #599 merge run is red, but from Desktop/Web E2E — **SDK E2E was never present** on it. So the Test 21 flake has never been observed on a main push; it can only surface on PRs that touch SDK-triggering paths.

Git history confirms Test 21 was added by `703bc0083` (#599, Phase 71): file comment line 2 reads *"Phase 66; Test 21 added Phase 71."*

## 4. Culprit-commit hypothesis

`703bc0083` "feat: enforce share-invite authorization and IPNS data-integrity in the API (#599)" — it added both the anti-equivocation/idempotency semantics in `apps/api/src/ipns/ipns.service.ts` and the Test 21 (D-06) assertion. The test asserts a strict "exactly one 409" outcome that the API's same-CID idempotency does not deterministically guarantee. Re-running #600's SDK E2E leg should pass (flake), while the underlying test/semantics mismatch remains a latent main issue that will resurface on any SDK-touching PR.

**Bottom line for #600:** safe to re-run / merge on this axis — the failure is orthogonal to its diff. The real follow-up (not for #600) is tightening Test 21 to use distinct CIDs, or making the first-publish loser deterministically 409 even on same-CID collisions.

<result>Windows fails identically — same test, same `.mts:295` POST /shares 400. Same root cause cross-OS.

## Diagnosis complete

**Exact 400: endpoint + reason**
- Endpoint: `POST /shares` (SharesController.createShare, `apps/api/src/shares/shares.controller.ts:40`).
- The API's global ValidationPipe runs `whitelist: true` + `forbidNonWhitelisted: true` (`apps/api/src/main.ts:22-23`). The request body carries unknown properties and is missing required ones, so NestJS returns 400 (`BadRequestException`) before the handler runs. Nest doesn't log the body, which is why `api.log` shows no error line — but the axios stack pins it to `shared-scope-exit-rotation.mts:295:22`, and the failure is immediate (0.0s), so it is the POST itself, not an IPNS publish.

**The offending call (test script, `tests/desktop-e2e/scripts/shared-scope-exit-rotation.mts:295-300`)**
```js
const shareRes = await axiosInstance.post('/shares', {
  recipientPublicKey: '0x' + bytesToHex(bobPublicKey),
  readDescriptorRef: bytesToHex(wrappedForBob),   // ← wrong field name
  rootNodeId: grantRootNodeId,
  rootIpnsName: grantRootIpnsName,                 // ← wrong field name
});
```
`CreateShareDto` (`apps/api/src/shares/dto/create-share.dto.ts`) requires `encryptedReadKey` (line 58) and `shareRootIpnsName` (line 91). The test sends the old names `readDescriptorRef` / `rootIpnsName`, which are (a) rejected as non-whitelisted and (b) leave the two required fields absent → 400.

Cause of the rename: commit **703bc0083 (#599)** did a module-wide rename in the shares domain — `readDescriptorRef → encryptedReadKey`, `writeDescriptorRef → encryptedWriteKey`, `rootIpnsName → shareRootIpnsName`. The `.mts` driver was never updated to match.

**Verdict: (b)** — the FUSE fix is correct and did NOT regress. It advanced the flow (the equivocation line is gone; `secret.txt` now appears via `pollFindChild`), which exposed a pre-existing, unrelated bug in the **test script**: it uses the old pre-#599 DTO field names. This is not (a) — there is no seq-1 IPNS equivocation in the script; the 400 is plain DTO validation. It is not (c) — nothing the CAS fall-through published is involved.

**Cross-OS:** Yes. Windows job 86265521723 fails at the identical point (`.mts:295`, 400 right after both `pollFindChild` successes). Same root cause.

**Minimal fix (test script only — no product code):** In `tests/desktop-e2e/scripts/shared-scope-exit-rotation.mts`:
1. Line ~295-300 POST body: rename `readDescriptorRef` → `encryptedReadKey` and `rootIpnsName` → `shareRootIpnsName`.
2. A second, latent break follows even after (1): lines 307-317 read the received share as `receivedShare.readDescriptorRef`. `ReceivedShareResponseDto` (`share-response.dto.ts:52`) now returns `encryptedReadKey` — so update the type annotation (line 309) and the `hexToBytes(receivedShare.readDescriptorRef)` at line 315 to `encryptedReadKey`, otherwise the Bob positive-control unwrap gets `undefined` and throws.

No API/DTO/FUSE change is warranted — the product contract (#599) is the intended one; only the desktop-e2e driver is stale. This is a pure test-fixture drift, same class as prior "SDK helper scripts drift after API rename" notes.</result>

1	//! Metadata encryption, merge, and background publish helpers.
2	
3	#[cfg(any(feature = "fuse", feature = "winfsp"))]
4	use std::sync::Arc;
5	#[cfg(any(feature = "fuse", feature = "winfsp"))]
6	use zeroize::Zeroizing;
7	
8	#[cfg(any(feature = "fuse", feature = "winfsp"))]
9	use cipherbox_api_client::ApiClient;
10	
11	#[cfg(any(feature = "fuse", feature = "winfsp"))]
12	use crate::publish::PublishCoordinator;
13	
14	/// Shared one-retry CAS publish helper (D-03).
15	///
16	/// Resolves the current IPNS sequence, calls `make_record(new_seq)` to produce
17	/// `(record_b64, metadata_cid)`, publishes with `expected_sequence_number:
18	/// Some(seq.to_string())`, and on `Conflict` re-resolves + retries once with a
19	/// jitter back-off.
20	///
21	/// On persistent `Conflict`:
22	/// - If `journal_entry: Some((queue, entry))` — enqueue via `WriteQueue::put` and
23	///   return `Ok(())` (durable ack). **No call site supplies `Some` this phase** — see
24	///   D-01a: there is no `JournalOp::FilePublish`/`BinPublish` variant in
25	///   `crates/sdk/src/queue.rs`, so journaling per-file/bin publishes is a deferred
26	///   cross-crate change (CONTEXT Deferred Ideas).
27	/// - If `journal_entry: None` — return `Err` (the fire-and-forget caller logs at
28	///   `log::error!` and the blocking/sync path returns `EIO`).
29	///
30	/// Hard failures (record creation, marshal, upload, resolve) propagate `Err`
31	/// immediately — no retry.
32	///
33	/// The `old_cids_to_unpin` parameter carries CIDs to unpin only on success; on the
34	/// retry path additional intermediate CIDs are also cleaned up. Pass `vec![]` when
35	/// there is nothing to unpin.
36	#[cfg(any(feature = "fuse", feature = "winfsp"))]
37	pub(crate) async fn publish_with_cas_retry<F>(
38	    api: &ApiClient,
39	    coordinator: &PublishCoordinator,
40	    ipns_name: &str,
41	    make_record: F,
42	    old_cids_to_unpin: &[String],
43	    journal_entry: Option<()>, // placeholder for future (queue, entry) — always None this phase
44	) -> Result<(), String>
45	where
46	    F: Fn(u64) -> Result<(String, String), String>, // make_record(new_seq) -> (record_b64, cid)
47	{
48	    let seq = coordinator.resolve_sequence(api, ipns_name).await?;
49	    let new_seq = seq
50	        .checked_add(1)
51	        .ok_or_else(|| "IPNS sequence number overflow".to_string())?;
52	
53	    let (record_b64, metadata_cid) = make_record(new_seq)?;
54	
55	    let req = cipherbox_api_client::IpnsPublishRequest {
56	        ipns_name: ipns_name.to_string(),
57	        record: record_b64,
58	        metadata_cid: metadata_cid.clone(),
59	        encrypted_ipns_private_key: None,
60	        key_epoch: None,
61	        expected_sequence_number: Some(seq.to_string()),
62	    };
63	
64	    match cipherbox_api_client::ipns::publish_ipns(api, &req)
65	        .await
66	        .map_err(|e| format!("{}", e))?
67	    {
68	        cipherbox_api_client::PublishResult::Success => {
69	            coordinator.record_publish(ipns_name, new_seq);
70	            for cid in old_cids_to_unpin {
71	                let _ = cipherbox_api_client::ipfs::unpin_content(api, cid).await;
72	            }
73	            return Ok(());
74	        }
75	        cipherbox_api_client::PublishResult::Conflict {
76	            current_sequence_number,
77	        } => {
78	            log::warn!(
79	                "Conflict for {}: expected seq {}, server has {}. Re-resolving for retry.",
80	                ipns_name,
81	                seq,
82	                current_sequence_number
83	            );
84	
85	            let jitter_ms = (std::time::SystemTime::now()
86	                .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
87	                .unwrap_or_default()
88	                .subsec_nanos()
89	                % 400) as u64
90	                + 100;

===== existing flake todo =====
---
created: 2026-06-24
title: Stabilize flaky web-e2e suite (cascade-abort ordering)
area: tests/web-e2e
files:

  - tests/web-e2e/tests/invite-link-workflow.spec.ts

> NOTE: The desktop-e2e macOS cross-client-**content**-sync leg of this todo
> (Test 5) is RESOLVED in PR #558 — see the "DONE" section at the bottom. The
> remaining actionable work here is the web-e2e cascade-abort below.

## Problem

The `tests/web-e2e` Playwright suite runs `workers: 1`, `fullyParallel: false`,
`retries: 0`, and aborts after a small number of failures. Because tests execute
sequentially in (alphabetical) file order, a flake in an *early* file skips every
later test as "did not run", so a single flaky test fails the whole suite and
hides the status of everything after it.

Observed flaky tests (intermittent, **pre-existing** — they predate Phase 60;
the pre-Phase-60 run 28043695361 failed on `media-preview` + `sharing-workflow`
1.1 account creation):

- `invite-link-workflow.spec.ts:157` — `1.1 Create test accounts (Alice, Dave, Eve)` (account-creation setup)
- `journey-timing.spec.ts:94` — `Journey 1: login-to-vault` (timing-sensitive)
- `media-preview.spec.ts:54` — `upload media fixtures`

Surfaced while shipping Phase 60 (PR #555): across three web-e2e dispatches the
failing test differed each run (writable-shares once it had a real bug, then
media-preview, then invite-link + journey-timing), and because `writable-shares`
sorts last it was repeatedly skipped — making it impossible to confirm a fix from
CI alone (had to run the spec locally to verify). Not merge-blocking: web-e2e is
not a required PR check (it only auto-runs on main push when web paths change).

## Solution

TBD — options, smallest-first:

1. Add a small `retries` count (e.g. 1-2) for known-flaky specs, or globally, so a
   single transient failure does not fail + truncate the run.
2. Stabilize the account-creation flow (`1.1 Create test accounts` in
   invite-link-workflow / sharing-workflow) — the Web3Auth mock login + first-publish
   timing is the most common flake source.
3. De-couple ordering so one early flake does not skip the rest (raise/remove the
   max-failures cap in CI, or shard independent specs), so a flaky test reports only
   itself rather than masking the whole tail.
4. Make `journey-timing` assertions tolerant of CI scheduling jitter (timing budgets).

Keep `retries: 0` philosophy in spirit (fix flakiness at the source) but stop a
single flake from masking unrelated coverage.

## RESOLVED 2026-06-25: macOS cross-client sync is a FUSE-T SMB-cache platform limit

CORRECTION: PR #558 (`mark_remotely_edited_files_unresolved`) was a real hardening
of the gated re-resolution path and it DOES engage — but it does NOT fix this flake.
The flake recurred on `main` AFTER #558 merged (run 28177924106, same Test 5
signature). The original "fixed by #558" claim was wrong.

True root cause (definitively pinned via a live local FUSE-T mount under
`RUST_LOG=debug` + a focused repro loop): the desktop's FUSE layer is CORRECT — on a
remote edit it detects the `modified_at` change and re-resolves the FilePointer to
the new CID within ~5s (logged: `DIAG: FilePointer ino N re-resolved to cid <newCid>
(size ..)`), via EITHER the non-gated `populate_folder` path OR #558's gated
`mark_remotely_edited_files_unresolved` path. The failure is entirely above FUSE: the
**macOS SMB client caches the file content and never re-calls FUSE `open`** for the
duration (~17 `cat`s, zero `open: ino=N`), serving the stale read. The mount is
`nonotification` and FUSE-T's SMB backend does **not** honor a FUSE `inval_inode`
reverse-notification — verified by an explicit experiment (refactored `mount2` →
`Session` + `Notifier`, called `inval_inode(ino,0,0)` after every re-resolution; the
log confirmed `inval_inode sent` immediately post-resolve, yet the SMB client STILL
served stale for 95s). So there is no reliable FUSE-side fix; the SMB cache TTL is
variable and intermittently exceeds the 120s budget (~15% on CI).

Resolution: **macOS-optional stopgap on Test 5** (`test-cross-client-sync.sh`),
mirroring the Test 7 rename leg — warn+pass on Darwin, still fail on Linux; the
`.ps1` (Windows) still enforces. #558 stays in as legitimate hardening (it correctly
re-resolves during a local-publish window and is the only unit-testable part).

Test 7 folder RENAME was already macOS-optional and fails for the SAME SMB cache
reason (the directory variant). Not separately actionable. A genuine fix for either
leg would require a FUSE-T/macOS-SMB change we don't control (e.g. SMB client cache
TTL tuning via mount options or `/etc/nsmb.conf`), tracked here if it ever matters.

Original analysis (kept for history — note its "gated branch" root-cause was only a
partial/secondary factor; the dominant cause is the SMB client cache above):

`tests/desktop-e2e/scripts/test-cross-client-sync.sh:194` —
`FUSE mount still shows original content after 120s` — flakes on **macOS only**
(Linux + Windows pass). Root cause is FUSE-T's SMB backend caching (noted in
`test-round-trip.sh:125`) stacked on the 30s IPNS poll: the test allows 120s
("two full polling cycles", line 172) for a cross-client write to surface in the
other client's FUSE mount, and on macOS the SMB cache occasionally exceeds that
window. The folder-rename leg is already marked "optional on macOS" for the same
reason (it warns instead of failing); the content-sync leg is not.

Evidence it is a flake, not a regression (PR #555 full CI E2E dispatch, run
28112732258 on commit 1f8f8d85d): the same macOS job PASSED on the immediately
prior full dispatch (run 28105996601, commit 88f096505), and `git diff
88f096505..1f8f8d85d` shows the ONLY Rust change is inside `crates/api-client/src/ipns.rs`
`mod tests` (skew boundary tests) — zero production-code delta in any path the
desktop binary exercises. macOS desktop also shows intermittent failures on `main`
history independent of this branch.

PROVEN pre-existing, NOT a Phase 60 regression (4-agent root-cause, high confidence):

Base rate (macOS desktop job, where it actually ran — dispatch-gated skips excluded):
- **main: ~15% fail on THIS test** — runs 28043695361 (job 83016343633) AND 27905000292
  (job 82572035159) both fail with the exact `Test 5 ... still shows original content
  after 120s` signature, BEFORE Phase 60. (2 other main macOS fails were a different
  ESM-loader infra break, not this test.) The rest pass (e.g. 28063779741 ALL PASSED).
- branch (1f8f8d85d): 1 fail / 3 pass across dispatches (28112732258 fail; 28105996601,
  28117194839, 28119647095 pass). Overlaps main's rate — no clear worsening.

Real root cause (`crates/fuse/src/fs.rs:392`, `drain_refresh_completions`):
```
if self.mutated_folders.contains_key(&ino) || self.publish_queue.contains_key(&ino) {
    self.metadata_cache.set(&ipns_name, metadata.clone(), cid);
    continue;  // caches remote edit but SKIPS populate_folder + the unresolved-
               // FilePointer resolve spawn that would fetch the new content
}
```
When the desktop is concurrently publishing its OWN changes (root ino sits in
`mutated_folders`/`publish_queue`, 30s retention), a refresh carrying the remote edit
takes this cache-only branch, so the per-file re-resolution is never spawned. The FUSE
read path only *polls* (`poll.rs:40` → NotInFlight unless a prior spawn inserted the ino;
`read_ops.rs:532` never spawns), so the file never re-resolves → original content for
120s → FAIL. It is timing-dependent (does the desktop's own publish window overlap the
remote-edit refresh?), hence flaky, and macOS runner timing makes the overlap likelier.

Decisively NOT Phase 60: `git diff origin/main...HEAD -- crates/fuse/src/fs.rs` = 4 ins /
13 del (ONLY re-pointing the resolve call to `cipherbox_api_client::ipns::resolve_ipns_verified`);
`inode.rs`/`read_ops.rs`/`poll.rs` are untouched. In the failing log `resolve_ipns_verified`
is NEVER called for the stuck file (no resolve / verify / 404 / success line for it — the
only 404 is an unrelated freshly-mkdir'd folder), so the strict-verify cutover cannot have
caused it. And the per-file record IS strict-verifiable (the SDK harness reports
`contentVerified:true` pre- and post-edit), ruling out a Phase 60 publish-side defect.
The `baseChildren ... union fallback` warning nearby is unrelated benign noise (present in
passing runs too).

Fix (separate desktop/FUSE PR — touches the delicate mutated_folders / folder-state-desync
logic, so NOT bundled into the IPNS verify cutover): in the cache-only `continue` branch,
still enqueue the parent's unresolved FilePointers for resolution (or defer a re-drain)
instead of dropping the remote-edit re-resolution, WITHOUT clobbering pending local
mutations with stale remote state (the reason the gate exists — see
[[project-web-sdk-folder-state-desync]]). Must pass SDK E2E + desktop E2E (all platforms).
A timeout bump is NOT a fix (the failure is a suppressed spawn, not slowness). The sibling
folder-rename leg is already "optional/warn on macOS"; making the content-sync leg the same
is only a test-hygiene stopgap, not the real fix.

reverse-notification — verified by an explicit experiment (refactored `mount2` →
`Session` + `Notifier`, called `inval_inode(ino,0,0)` after every re-resolution; the
log confirmed `inval_inode sent` immediately post-resolve, yet the SMB client STILL
served stale for 95s). So there is no reliable FUSE-side fix; the SMB cache TTL is
variable and intermittently exceeds the 120s budget (~15% on CI).

Resolution: **macOS-optional stopgap on Test 5** (`test-cross-client-sync.sh`),
mirroring the Test 7 rename leg — warn+pass on Darwin, still fail on Linux; the
`.ps1` (Windows) still enforces. #558 stays in as legitimate hardening (it correctly
re-resolves during a local-publish window and is the only unit-testable part).

Test 7 folder RENAME was already macOS-optional and fails for the SAME SMB cache
reason (the directory variant). Not separately actionable. A genuine fix for either
leg would require a FUSE-T/macOS-SMB change we don't control (e.g. SMB client cache
TTL tuning via mount options or `/etc/nsmb.conf`), tracked here if it ever matters.

Original analysis (kept for history — note its "gated branch" root-cause was only a
partial/secondary factor; the dominant cause is the SMB client cache above):

`tests/desktop-e2e/scripts/test-cross-client-sync.sh:194` —
`FUSE mount still shows original content after 120s` — flakes on **macOS only**
(Linux + Windows pass). Root cause is FUSE-T's SMB backend caching (noted in
`test-round-trip.sh:125`) stacked on the 30s IPNS poll: the test allows 120s
("two full polling cycles", line 172) for a cross-client write to surface in the
other client's FUSE mount, and on macOS the SMB cache occasionally exceeds that
window. The folder-rename leg is already marked "optional on macOS" for the same
reason (it warns instead of failing); the content-sync leg is not.

Evidence it is a flake, not a regression (PR #555 full CI E2E dispatch, run
28112732258 on commit 1f8f8d85d): the same macOS job PASSED on the immediately
prior full dispatch (run 28105996601, commit 88f096505), and `git diff
88f096505..1f8f8d85d` shows the ONLY Rust change is inside `crates/api-client/src/ipns.rs`
`mod tests` (skew boundary tests) — zero production-code delta in any path the
desktop binary exercises. macOS desktop also shows intermittent failures on `main`
history independent of this branch.

PROVEN pre-existing, NOT a Phase 60 regression (4-agent root-cause, high confidence):

Base rate (macOS desktop job, where it actually ran — dispatch-gated skips excluded):
- **main: ~15% fail on THIS test** — runs 28043695361 (job 83016343633) AND 27905000292

  after 120s` signature, BEFORE Phase 60. (2 other main macOS fails were a different
  ESM-loader infra break, not this test.) The rest pass (e.g. 28063779741 ALL PASSED).
- branch (1f8f8d85d): 1 fail / 3 pass across dispatches (28112732258 fail; 28105996601,
  28117194839, 28119647095 pass). Overlaps main's rate — no clear worsening.

```
if self.mutated_folders.contains_key(&ino) || self.publish_queue.contains_key(&ino) {
    self.metadata_cache.set(&ipns_name, metadata.clone(), cid);
    continue;  // caches remote edit but SKIPS populate_folder + the unresolved-
               // FilePointer resolve spawn that would fetch the new content
}
```
When the desktop is concurrently publishing its OWN changes (root ino sits in
`mutated_folders`/`publish_queue`, 30s retention), a refresh carrying the remote edit
takes this cache-only branch, so the per-file re-resolution is never spawned. The FUSE
read path only *polls* (`poll.rs:40` → NotInFlight unless a prior spawn inserted the ino;
`read_ops.rs:532` never spawns), so the file never re-resolves → original content for
120s → FAIL. It is timing-dependent (does the desktop's own publish window overlap the
remote-edit refresh?), hence flaky, and macOS runner timing makes the overlap likelier.

13 del (ONLY re-pointing the resolve call to `cipherbox_api_client::ipns::resolve_ipns_verified`);
`inode.rs`/`read_ops.rs`/`poll.rs` are untouched. In the failing log `resolve_ipns_verified`
is NEVER called for the stuck file (no resolve / verify / 404 / success line for it — the
only 404 is an unrelated freshly-mkdir'd folder), so the strict-verify cutover cannot have
caused it. And the per-file record IS strict-verifiable (the SDK harness reports
`contentVerified:true` pre- and post-edit), ruling out a Phase 60 publish-side defect.
The `baseChildren ... union fallback` warning nearby is unrelated benign noise (present in
passing runs too).

logic, so NOT bundled into the IPNS verify cutover): in the cache-only `continue` branch,
still enqueue the parent's unresolved FilePointers for resolution (or defer a re-drain)
instead of dropping the remote-edit re-resolution, WITHOUT clobbering pending local
mutations with stale remote state (the reason the gate exists — see
[[project-web-sdk-folder-state-desync]]). Must pass SDK E2E + desktop E2E (all platforms).

folder-rename leg is already "optional/warn on macOS"; making the content-sync leg the same
is only a test-hygiene stopgap, not the real fix.

Given a retry or more time, the editor would load the restored content.

This points to a **test-timing flake** (the e2e reopens the editor before the restore's IPNS republish is visible to the resolve endpoint), **not** a missing cache invalidation in the restore handler. One caveat worth noting for the test: the restore handler intentionally does **not** refresh the open folder listing at all (only quota + the details dialog's own version list). If the e2e also asserts the *file list* reflects post-restore size/mtime, that WOULD be a genuine missing-invalidation gap (`useFileVersions.handleRestoreVersion` never refreshes the folder store). But for the specific editor-content symptom described, the editor path is fresh-resolve and the flake is timing.</result>

52

59	        encrypted_ipns_private_key: None,

---

## Test 1 — `full-workflow.spec.ts:1314 › 6.6.2 Restore a past version` (run 29061952925)

**Exact failure** (job 86265524185 log line 35035):
```
Error: expect(received).toBe(expected)   // line 1355
Expected: "Updated content after edit - version 2"
Received: "Edited in-browser via text editor modal - version 3"
```
The trace shows: restore-confirm clicked → details closed → editor opened → textarea read immediately. The editor showed the **pre-restore** current content (version 3).

**Root cause — missing synchronization (not stale cache).** The only "wait" between confirming the restore and reading the editor is (lines 1476-1478):
```ts
await expect(async () => {
  expect(await detailsDialog.getVersionCount()).toBe(1);
}).toPass({ timeout: 30000 });
```
Restore **swaps** current↔v1, so the past-version count is `1` **both before and after** restore. This gate passes instantly and provides **zero** wait for the restore's IPNS republish to land. I confirmed via a sub-agent that the text editor re-resolves the file **fresh from the live API on every open** (`downloadFromIpns` → `resolveIpnsRecord` → `resolveFileMetadata` → `downloadFileContent`, none cached — `packages/sdk/src/client.ts:4169`, `packages/sdk-core/src/ipns/index.ts:196`, `.../file/index.ts:373`). So there is no in-memory current-CID for restore to invalidate; the editor simply raced the just-committed/in-flight restore publish and read the old record. Given more time it reads version 2.

**Classification: (A) fixable test-timing race.**

**Fix** — full-workflow.spec.ts tail of 6.6.2 (~lines 1483-1495). The trivial `getVersionCount()===1` gate is a no-op; replace the single open→read→assert with a poll of the real end-state:
```ts
await expect
  .poll(async () => {
    await fileList.rightClickItem(editableFileName);
    await contextMenu.waitForOpen();
    await contextMenu.clickEdit();
    await textEditorDialog.waitForOpen({ timeout: 10000 });
    await textEditorDialog.waitForContentLoaded({ timeout: 30000 });
    const c = await textEditorDialog.getContent();
    await textEditorDialog.clickCancel();
    await textEditorDialog.waitForClose();
    return c;
  }, { timeout: 30000 })
  .toBe(editableFileUpdatedContent);
```
Note `textEditorDialog.waitForContentLoaded` (`text-editor-dialog.page.ts:100`) only waits for the textarea to be *visible*, not for correct content — so a single read is inherently racy.

**Latent product gap to flag separately (not what broke this test):** `useFileVersions.handleRestoreVersion` (`apps/web/src/hooks/useFileVersions.ts:58`) never refreshes the open folder listing after restore — only quota + the details dialog's own version list (`DetailsDialog.tsx:178` just bumps `metadataRefresh`). The file list won't show restored size/mtime until the 30s sync poll. Worth a ticket, but orthogonal to this flake.

---

## Test 2 — `writable-shares.spec.ts:533 › 8.1 Owner can navigate into subfolder created by recipient` (run 29061952925)

**Exact failure** (log line 35065):
```
TimeoutError: locator.waitFor: Timeout 30000ms exceeded.   // line 544
> 544 | await bobSharedBrowser.getFolderItem(securitySubfolder).waitFor({ state: 'visible', timeout: 30000 })
```
Bob (recipient) does an `--mkdir` in a **writable shared folder**, then waits ≤30s for the folder to render in his own view. Immediately preceded by 7.2 (Bob deletes a subfolder) — so back-to-back shared-writes on the same folder IPNS.

**Root cause — tighter timeout on the highest-latency path.** A recipient mkdir in a shared folder is a full shared-write → IPNS publish → re-resolve/refresh round-trip; under 3-worker load on the shared Kubo it can exceed 30s (it *does* eventually render — slow, not broken). Critically, the whole `writable-shares` spec and the `SharedFileBrowser` page object use **bare `waitFor({timeout:30000})` with no CI floor**, while `FileListPage` waiters apply `ciFloor` → 60s on CI (`page-objects/file-browser/file-list.page.ts:10-16, 120, 130`). So the shared path — where write latency is *highest* — is held to *half* the budget of the equivalent owner path.

**Classification: (A) with a (C) tail** — a timeout-calibration miss layered on genuinely slow-but-correct shared-write IPNS latency (the exact reason the 60s floor exists).

**Fix** — bump the shared appear-waits to the 60s floor. Minimal: change the two shared-mkdir waits in `writable-shares.spec.ts` (line 544 for `securitySubfolder`, and the 8.2 `deepSubfolder` at line 597) from `timeout: 30000` → `60000`. Systemic (preferred): add a floored `waitForFolderItem(name, opts)` to `shared-file-browser.page.ts` mirroring `FileListPage`'s `ciFloor`+`waitForItemToAppear`, and route the spec's shared appear-waits (lines 65, 87, 214, 233, 544, 597 …) through it so every shared-write wait gets the same 60s CI floor.

---

## Test 3 — `full-workflow.spec.ts:1456 › 8.2 Delete remaining root files` (run 29062823570)

**Exact failure** (job 86268131289 log line 38444):
```
Test timeout of 90000ms exceeded.
```
Error-context DOM = **empty directory** (all files deleted). Trace confirms all 3 delete cycles ran to completion (renamed → config → editable: rightClick → Delete → confirm → wait-gone).

**Root cause — cumulative budget overflow.** 8.2 deletes 3 files sequentially via `deleteItem` (full-workflow.spec.ts:295), each doing `confirmDialog.waitForClose(15s)` + `waitForItemToDisappear({timeout:15000})` — and `ciFloor` raises that disappearance wait to a **60s cap on CI**. Each delete is a separate IPNS publish→refresh round-trip. **8.2 has no `test.setTimeout`, so it runs under the default 90s CI budget.** Three serial IPNS-gated deletes under 3-worker load cumulatively blew past 90s even though each individually succeeded. The per-item waiters are correct; the *test budget* is too small. (The config comment at `playwright.config.ts:31-36` already names "multi-mutation deletes" as the load-sensitive path that forced workers 4→3.)

**Classification: (A/C boundary) — cumulative-timeout flake.** Underlying per-delete latency is irreducible live-stack (C); the fix is test-level (A).

**Fix** — pick one:
- **Minimal:** add `test.setTimeout(150000)` to 8.2 (mirrors 6.6.2 and writable 8.1 which already raise their budgets).
- **Better (philosophy-aligned):** collapse 3 round-trips into 1 — select-all then bulk-delete via the selection bar. Page objects already support it: the header "Select all" checkbox (used in test 4.4) + `selectionBar.clickDelete()` (`selection-action-bar.page.ts:105`) → one confirm → one IPNS round-trip, comfortably under 90s.

---

## Suite-level: should CI add `retries: 1`?

**Primary recommendation: fix all three at source first — do not reach for retries.** All three are fully diagnosable; none is Web3Auth/irreducible jitter. Two are pure timeout calibration (add the missing CI floor / raise the budget or bulk the operation), one is a genuinely absent wait. Papering these with retries would hide exactly the kind of fixable timing bug the `retries:0` philosophy is meant to surface.

**Secondary (defensible backstop, optional):** the substrate *is* a shared 2-vCPU stack whose IPNS publish/resolve latency has a fat tail under 3-worker load — that tail will keep producing occasional cumulative/timeout blips on other multi-mutation paths. A **CI-only `retries: 1`** (not 2) is a reasonable safety net *because Playwright reports retried tests as "flaky" in the run summary* — visible, not hidden. A genuinely-broken test still fails both attempts and reds the build; a transient live-stack blip passes on retry and lands in the flaky list for triage. That preserves the fix-at-source signal while cutting spurious red builds. If you adopt it: `retries: process.env.CI ? 1 : 0`, keep local at 0, and make "any test in the flaky report is a must-fix" a standing rule. I'd gate this on fixing the current three first and only add it if residual flakiness remains.

**Recommended order:** (1) land the three source fixes above; (2) re-run the dispatched suite twice; (3) add `retries:1` CI-only *only if* still flaky, with the flaky-report-triage rule.</result>

skills.name: gsd-plan-phase
skills.content:
<objective>
Create executable phase prompts (PLAN.md files) for a roadmap phase with integrated research and verification.

**Default flow:** Research (if needed) → Plan → Verify → Done

**Research-only mode (`--research-phase <N>`):** Spawn `gsd-phase-researcher` for phase `N`, write `RESEARCH.md`, then exit before the planner runs. Useful for cross-phase research, doc review before committing to a planning approach, and correction-without-replanning loops where iterating on research alone is dramatically cheaper than re-spawning the planner. Replaces the deleted research-phase command (#3042).

**Research-only modifiers:**
- **No flag** — when `RESEARCH.md` already exists, auto-uses it: emits a one-line notice and exits cleanly, no prompt.
- **`--research`** — force-refresh: re-spawn the researcher unconditionally, no prompt. Bypasses the existing-RESEARCH.md auto-use path.
- **`--view`** — view-only: print existing `RESEARCH.md` to stdout. Does not spawn the researcher. Cheapest mode for the correction-without-replanning loop. If no `RESEARCH.md` exists yet, errors with a hint to drop `--view`.

**Orchestrator role:** Parse arguments, validate phase, research domain (unless skipped), spawn gsd-planner, verify with gsd-plan-checker, iterate until pass or max iterations, present results.
</objective>

They are equivalent — `vscode_askquestions` is the VS Code Copilot implementation of the same interactive question API. Do not skip questioning steps because `AskUserQuestion` appears unavailable; use `vscode_askquestions` instead.
</runtime_note>

Phase number: 72 (optional — auto-detects next unplanned phase if omitted)

**Flags:**
- `--research` — Force re-research even if RESEARCH.md exists
- `--skip-research` — Skip research, go straight to planning
- `--gaps` — Gap closure mode (reads VERIFICATION.md, skips research)
- `--skip-verify` — Skip verification loop
- `--prd <file>` — Use a PRD/acceptance criteria file instead of discuss-phase. Parses requirements into CONTEXT.md automatically. Skips discuss-phase entirely.
- `--ingest <path-or-glob>` — Use one or more ADR files instead of discuss-phase. Parses locked decisions + scope fences into CONTEXT.md automatically. Skips discuss-phase entirely.
- `--ingest-format <auto|nygard|madr|narrative>` — Optional ADR parser format override (`auto` default).
- `--reviews` — Replan incorporating cross-AI review feedback from REVIEWS.md (produced by `/gsd-review`)
- `--text` — Use plain-text numbered lists instead of TUI menus (required for `/rc` remote sessions)
- `--mvp` — Vertical MVP mode. Planner organizes tasks as feature slices (UI→API→DB) instead of horizontal layers. On Phase 1 of a new project, also emits `SKELETON.md` (Walking Skeleton). Can be persisted on a phase via `**Mode:** mvp` in ROADMAP.md.

Normalize phase input in step 2 before any directory lookups.
</context>
