input.content:
## Phase 72 — SDK Write-Plane Durability and Correctness

Makes the SDK write plane sound on delete/move/restore/replace, fails closed instead of sealing an empty write-body, keeps folder listings fresh after in-place edits, removes a latent wrong-key branch, and consolidates the duplicated write-plane helpers — with the test suite hardened and CI now typechecking test files.

### Success criteria (all verified — see `72-VERIFICATION.md`)

- **SC#1 — delete drops the WriteChildRef.** `deleteItem` resolves the removed child's node **UUID** (not its ipnsName) before trimming `writeChildren`, so the write-chain no longer grows unbounded. The `updateFolderMetadataAndPublish` CAS-merge is now **base-aware**: a concurrent write can no longer resurrect a just-dropped write-link.
- **SC#2 — fail-closed `getWriteBodyParams`.** A transient IPNS resolve miss while a real writeKey is present now throws (naming the folder) instead of sealing `writeChildren: []` and silently discarding the chain. The legitimate zero-writeKey read-only path is unchanged. Applied to both the client and the CLI copies.
- **SC#3 — restore re-homing.** `restoreFromBin` to a *different* parent reseals the `WriteChildRef` under the destination write scope (dest-before-source), reusing the shipped `moveItem` pattern; `permanentDeleteFromBin` drops the lingering original-parent link.
- **SC#4 — fresh listings after an edit.** In-place edits now invalidate the folder `listingCache` (the shipped `updateSharedFile` one-liner), rather than reintroducing the `SealedChildRef` size/mtime mirror that was reverted in `68.2-12`. No extra parent publish.
- **SC#5 — dead branch removed.** The unreachable `moveInSharedFolder` `shareKeys.length > 0` branch (which assigned an Ed25519 `ipnsPrivateKey` as an AES `destWriteKey`) and its `getShareKeysFn` param are gone; web callers updated. A previously `describe.skip`'d regression test now gates the removal.
- **SC#6 — helper consolidation.** A single `walkChildWriteKey(mode)` primitive (string-literal mode union) unifies the write-chain hop-walk sites; single `hasRealWriteKey` predicate; `wrapIpnsKeyForTee` extracted for the 3 triplicated TEE-enrollment gates; shared `write-body-params.ts` (the CLI twin now delegates); `runFileVersionOp` shared version-op core. `write-chain-rotation.test.ts` identifies rotated seeds by provenance; `upload-batch.test.ts` mocks use the current `SealedChildRef` shape.

### Also in this PR (test + CI hardening)

- **All test files now typecheck in CI.** Previously `pnpm typecheck` only built production code (`tsconfig.build.json` excludes tests), so test-file type drift was invisible. Added a test-inclusive `typecheck` script per package, chained into the root `typecheck` (build-first). Fixed the pre-existing drift this exposed: a vitest v2→v3 `Mock` generics migration (api-client, sdk-core) and a Phase-62 retired-type migration across 12 sdk test files — no `as any`/`@ts-ignore`, no weakened assertions.
- **Stale skips resolved.** The 36 skipped sdk tests marked `TODO(phase 63/65)` (both already shipped) are down to 3: five blocks migrated to the Node/v3 model and enabled, one obsolete-by-redesign block removed, and the live-API `integration.test.ts` suite kept as a documented infra gate.
- **DoS-class fix surfaced by the hardening.** `collectDescendantIpnsNames` (unenroll/unpin subtree walk) had no cycle guard, so a cyclic/malicious folder graph recursed unbounded. Now threads the same `visited` set `dfsFindFolder` uses, with coverage.

### Verification

- Unit: `@cipherbox/sdk` 412 passed / 3 skipped / 0 failed; `@cipherbox/sdk-core` 366 passed. The 3 remaining skips are the live-API integration suite.
- `pnpm typecheck` (now test-inclusive) green across all packages; production builds clean; `web tsc -b` clean.
- **Live sdk-e2e (real IPNS round-trip):** 15 suites / 104 tests passed — folder-crud, concurrent-operations, bin-operations (incl. the SC#3 restore-to-different-parent proof), write-chain-rotation, and the read/share/vault suites. The only failures were `tee-republish` (2), which require a seeded `tee_key_state` table this phase does not touch — an environment gap, green in CI.

### Residuals (non-blocking)

- web-e2e (writable-shares / move-restore) for the SC#6 high-blast-radius refactor is dispatched against this branch before merge (unit + live sdk-e2e already gate it).
- SC#4's list-refresh is unit-proven; a manual browser confirmation is the only un-exercised path.

<result># Security Review — Phase 72 (SDK Write-Plane Durability)

**Scope reviewed:** `git diff origin/main...HEAD` for `packages/sdk/src`, `packages/sdk-core/src`, `packages/core/src` (network access to refresh `origin/main` was unavailable, but the local `origin/main` ref plus full branch history was accessible and used). Read files in full where the diff alone was insufficient: `client.ts`, `bin/index.ts`, `write-body-params.ts`, `registration.ts`, `wrap.ts`, plus `.planning/phases/72-*` research/plan/summary docs to check whether gaps found were already known/deferred.

## Summary of verified-correct items

- **D-09 zeroization (item 1):** `walkChildWriteKey`, `hasRealWriteKey`, `wrapIpnsKeyForTee` are pure borrows — none mutate/zero caller-owned buffers. `walkChildWriteKey` follows the "null-before-return, zero-only-in-finally-on-throw" idiom correctly at every one of its ~8 call sites (`packages/sdk/src/client.ts:93-107`); no double-zero, no use-after-zero found. `runFileVersionOp` (`client.ts:570-626`) preserves the original triplicated finally block exactly (zeroes `fileReadKey`/`fileWriteKey`/`fileIpnsPrivateKey` unconditionally). The `updateSharedSingleFile` fix (`client.ts:5449-5537`) genuinely closes the leak: both `unwrapKey` calls are now inside the `try`, null-initialized outside it, so a throw on the second call still reaches the same unconditional `finally` and zeroes the already-unwrapped first key.
- **Fail-closed correctness (item 2):** `getWriteBodyParams` (`packages/sdk/src/write-body-params.ts:699-721`) is now a single shared implementation used by both `client.ts` and `bin/index.ts` — the "two copies could disagree" risk (SC#2) is structurally eliminated, not just kept in sync. The zero/absent-writeKey short-circuit (`if (!hasRealWriteKey(wk)) return {}`) happens *before* the resolve-and-throw branch, so the fail-closed throw only fires for folders that actually have a real writeKey — the read-only-device availability path is unaffected. Verified correct.
- **Key-type confusion removal (item 3, SC#5):** The `moveInSharedFolder` `shareKeys.length > 0` legacy branch and `getShareKeysFn` param are fully removed from `client.ts`/`share/shared-write.ts`'s public signature. Grepped both web callers (`apps/web/src/hooks/useSharedWriteOps.ts`) — neither passes a residual `getShareKeysFn`; no dangling caller.
- **Cycle guard (item 5):** `collectDescendantIpnsNames`'s `visited` Set (`client.ts:459-494`) is marked synchronously before any `await`, shared by reference across all recursive calls and all three root call sites (each seeded with the root's own ipnsName). This correctly bounds total recursion to the number of distinct ipnsNames ever seen, terminating on any cyclic/malicious folder graph. Verified correct — no DoS vector.
- **Write-chain integrity for `deleteItem` / `restoreFromBin` / `permanentDeleteFromBin` (item 4, partial):** the base-aware CAS-merge in `registration.ts:332-367` correctly prunes a childId present in `baseWriteChildren` but absent from local, even when a racing writer's stale remote snapshot still carries it, while still admitting genuinely concurrent remote-only adds. `deleteItem` (`client.ts:2978-3057`) and both `bin/index.ts` re-homing paths thread `baseWriteChildren` through correctly. `restoreFromBin`'s cross-folder re-home reseals the moved item's writeKey under the **destination** writeKey (`bin/index.ts` `sealChildWriteKey(movedWriteKey, targetWriteBodyParams.writeKey, ...)`), not the source — correct, matches the requirement. Dest-before-source publish ordering is preserved (crash never fully orphans write capability).

## Findings

### [HIGH] `moveItem` never threads `baseWriteChildren` — its own source-folder WriteChildRef drop can be resurrected by a concurrent writer

**Location:** `packages/sdk/src/client.ts:2916-2932` (source-folder publish inside `moveItem`), merge logic at `packages/sdk-core/src/folder/registration.ts:332-367`

**Code:**
```typescript
// client.ts moveItem — SOURCE folder publish (drops the moved child's WriteChildRef)
const { newSequenceNumber: srcSeq, publishedChildren: srcChildren, publishedWriteChildren: srcPublishedWriteChildren } =
  await sdkCore.updateFolderMetadataAndPublish({
    children: updatedSource,
    baseChildren: baseSourceChildren,
    readKey: sourceFolder.folderKey,
    writeKey: sourceWriteBodyParams.writeKey,
    writeChildren: rehomedSourceWriteChildren,   // <- has the moved child's ref REMOVED
    // no baseWriteChildren passed here
    ...
  });
```

**Issue:**
`moveItem` drops the moved child's `WriteChildRef` from the source folder's write-body (`rehomedSourceWriteChildren = sourceWriteBodyParams.writeChildren.filter(wc => wc.childId !== childPub.id)`, `client.ts:2859-2861`) — structurally the same operation `deleteItem` performs. But unlike `deleteItem` (which this same phase fixed), `moveItem` never passes `baseWriteChildren` to `updateFolderMetadataAndPublish`. Per `registration.ts:340-367`, when `params.baseWriteChildren` is `undefined` the merge falls back to the "legacy naive union" (`byChildId.set` for local then remote, remote entries always win/are always included) — the exact premise the phase's own research doc (`72-RESEARCH.md` "Critical Finding 2") states will resurrect a dropped `WriteChildRef` under a concurrent-write race.

If a CAS-409 occurs on the source-folder publish (a racing writer — another collaborator or another device of the same user in a shared folder — republishes the source folder from a snapshot that predates the move), the retry's naive union re-adds the racing writer's stale `WriteChildRef` for the moved child back into the source folder's write-body, even though `moveItem` explicitly intended to drop it.

This is not a newly-introduced bug in the sense of being unknown — the phase's own `72-03-SUMMARY.md:33,120` explicitly documents it: *"other write-chain callers (`moveItem`, `restoreFromBin`) do not yet pass it and continue to get the pre-existing naive-union behavior... SC#3 (restoreFromBin re-homing, deferred to Plan 05) is the next candidate to thread it through."* Plan 05 threaded it through for `restoreFromBin`/`permanentDeleteFromBin`, but no subsequent plan in this phase (checked 72-01 through 72-10 PLAN/SUMMARY docs) revisited `moveItem`. `72-VERIFICATION.md:31` marks SC#1 "VERIFIED" citing only `deleteItem`, with no mention of the residual `moveItem` exposure. There is no pending todo tracking it (`.planning/todos/pending` has nothing referencing `moveItem` + the naive-union gap). There is also no regression test for it (`move-in-shared-folder.test.ts` has no concurrent/409/resurrection test).

**Impact:**
In a shared folder with multiple writers (or a single user with multiple devices holding a real writeKey for the same folder), after Alice moves file/folder F out of source folder S into destination D, a concurrent stale republish of S can resurrect F's `WriteChildRef` in S. F then becomes write-capable via **two** independent write scopes simultaneously — the new destination D (intended) and the old source S (unintended). Anyone who retains write access to S (which may include a collaborator whose access to F was specifically supposed to end when it was moved out of the folder they can write to) can still mutate F using S's writeKey, even though F no longer appears in S's read-plane children — a live, silently-restored write capability outside the intended sharing/authorization boundary.
